title.en: Experienced trainers with divided client feedback

text.en: Many dog owners commend Dean Miller, Dallas, and the Club Canine team for their deep knowledge of canine behavior and structured instruction. Satisfied clients appreciate their patient guidance with stubborn or high-energy breeds. However, critical reviewers report negative experiences, citing aggressive interactions, unreturned phone calls, and disputes regarding upfront payments.

title.en: Substantial obedience gains and certification success

text.en: Most reviewers report remarkable progress in canine behavior, from basic puppy manners to advanced off-leash obedience, gundog work, and Canine Good Citizen titles. Owners of reactive or high-drive dogs highlight significant improvements in impulse control and daily handling. A critical reviewer discontinued sessions abruptly due to harsh training methods.

title.en: High-drive dog focus alongside handling controversy

text.en: Several reviewers note that trainers excel at understanding working breeds and managing driven dogs that failed in treat-only classes. Clients appreciate that staff work through complex behavioral patterns. In contrast, one highly critical reviewer reported alarming physical leash corrections and injuries, warning potential clients against intense training methods.

q.en: Does Club Canine work with high-drive and working breeds?

a.en: Yes, trainers frequently work with high-drive breeds such as Dobermans, Labradors, and hunting dogs on advanced obedience.

q.en: Are dogs prepared for Canine Good Citizen certification?

a.en: Yes, clients note that the training curriculum prepares dogs for Canine Good Citizen (CGC) testing and higher certifications.
Reviews describe balanced, structured training techniques for obedience, though some reviewers noted strict physical leash handling.
